source.title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model's Perception of the World at Any Resolution
source.authors: Peng Wang; Shuai Bai; Sinan Tan; Shijie Wang; Zhihao Fan; Jinze Bai; Keqin Chen; Xuejing Liu; Jialin Wang; Wenbin Ge; Yang Fan; Kai Dang; Mengfei Du; Xuancheng Ren; Rui Men; Dayiheng Liu; Chang Zhou; Jingren Zhou; Junyang Lin

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream benchmark performance across model sizes and training-token amounts in vision-language models, conceptually testing downstream scaling trends. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy or fit power laws.
record.gate_note: Figure 6 reports scaling sweeps relevant to V6. The benchmark comparisons elsewhere in the paper are not scaling sweeps and are not recorded as rows. No cross-entropy, power-law fit, small-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation result is reported.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (vision-language models built on Qwen2 LLMs), Section 3.3.3 / Figure 6 reports downstream benchmark scores across three model sizes (2B, 7B, 72B) and across training tokens for the 7B model. This bears on V6 only, and weakly: three sizes show direction but not predictability. No loss, power-law fit, extrapolation or allocation result is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors frame Section 3.3.3 as exploring scaling laws for LVLMs and report consistent improvement with model size, especially math, while noting small models are already strong on OCR tasks. With more second-stage training tokens, the 7B model improves, with fluctuation on VQA and steady gains on AI2D and InfoVQA. No law is fitted.
record.recipe_differences: This is an LVLM benchmark scaling study: it compares aggregate downstream performance across three model sizes and tracks selected scores during a training-token sweep, rather than fitting held-out language-model loss laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports some fluctuation for VQA during the training-token sweep; AI2D and InfoVQA improve steadily.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The study reports benchmark performance, not held-out cross-entropy or fitted power-law predictions; it provides no uncertainty estimates for the scaling curves.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-related results left out. Other benchmark comparison tables are excluded because they compare final models rather than report scaling sweeps.

untested.parts: No held-out loss or power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law form is fitted for vision-language training.
Predictability is untested: there is no functional fit and only three sizes, so the study shows direction only. No link to pretraining loss.
No fitting or setup dependence is examined.

missing.what: Per-size numeric benchmark scores that make the Figure 6(a) size trend readable (MMMU, MathVista, MathVision, DocVQA, OCRBench, MMStar, etc.).
Per-size video benchmark scores (MVBench, PerceptionTest, EgoSchema, Video-MME).
Per-size referring-expression scores (RefCOCO etc.), monotonic with size.

record.verdict_notes: This is a model release report whose scaling evidence is three released sizes plus one token sweep, with no uncertainty. I set T3 rather than T2 because the system kind (VLM with a shared 675M ViT and Qwen2 LLMs initialised from pretrained checkpoints) differs from the claim's text-only language models. The size comparison is also confounded by the LLM backbone differing in size and pretraining. The rows split each comparison into per-model rows; the states describe the comparison as a whole.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy and power-law behavior in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on small runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation under a fixed compute budget.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether a power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
The study reports performance trends, but does not establish calibrated predictions from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or optimal allocations on fitting/setup choices, and bending of fitted curves.

relationships.condition: Model-size sweep 2B/7B/72B on college-level, math, general QA and video aggregates
relationships.reason: Scores rise monotonically with size (e.g. MMMU 41.1/54.1/64.5; MathVista 43.0/58.2/70.5), per Figure 6(a) and Tables 2 and 4; rows r1–r6 and r10–r15.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased monotonically with size, including MMMU from 41.1 to 54.1 to 64.5 and MathVista from 43.0 to 58.2 to 70.5.

relationships.reason: Gains are small or near saturation (DocVQA 90.1→96.5; OCRBench 809→877), and authors note small models are already strong; rows r7–r9.
relationships.display_finding: DocVQA increased from 90.1 to 96.5 and OCRBench from 809 to 877, with small models already performing strongly.

relationships.display_finding: AI2D and InfoVQA performance improved steadily with additional training tokens.
